text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for testing a citation checker.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, the Harrowfield Community Trust delivered monthly cash transfers to 1,240 households across the Marrel Valley. Village committees selected recipient households using a simple vulnerability score. Each household received 45 dollars per month, which recipients mostly spent on maize, beans and cooking oil. By December, 68% of participating families reported eating three meals a day, up from 41% at baseline. Transfers were not interrupted during the lean season, despite fuel shortages that delayed two distributions elsewhere in the district. We did not expand to the upland settlements this year because road access remained unsafe after the October floods.

passages.source_passage: This update covers the Lanthorn Evening Classes network from January to June 2024. Our 18 volunteer tutors ran classes in six community halls across Bressingham and Odley. Average attendance reached 212 learners a week, and 74% of those enrolled in January completed the first reading assessment. Learners mentored newer tutors during peer sessions, which the board approved in March. We did not secure a venue in Odley North, so twenty-three people remain on the waiting list. Three classes were cancelled in February when the Brook Street hall lost heating. No learner has been charged a fee, and the board should note that printing costs rose by about a third.

passages.source_passage: During 2023, the Kivumbe District Health Partnership trained 96 community health workers in eleven villages around Lake Nyamira. Each worker visited an average of 30 households per month, screening children for malnutrition and referring pregnant women to the Rusasa health centre. Facility deliveries rose from 52% to 71% over the year. Health workers supported nurses at monthly outreach clinics, which reached 4,300 people. The programme did not meet its target for tuberculosis referrals, largely because the district laboratory was closed for repairs between May and August. Stipends were never paid late, and no worker left the programme for financial reasons.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring visits in the third quarter of 2024 covered 54 savings groups supported by the Tamsin Rural Finance Collective in Oberra and Lisk counties. Total group savings reached 38,600 dollars, an increase of 19% since the previous quarter. Members repaid loans on time in most groups, and the average loan size was eighty-five dollars. Group treasurers trained new members in record keeping during the August meetings. Four groups did not hold their share-out on schedule because of disputes over late contributions. Field staff found no evidence of missing funds, although two cash boxes lacked a third key holder.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation reviewed the Saltmere Coast Early Warning Programme between April 2022 and March 2024. The programme installed 14 sirens and trained 320 volunteers in nineteen fishing villages. During the November 2023 cyclone drill, 82% of households reached a designated shelter within forty minutes. Volunteers warned village elders before the drill, and elders then alerted families by radio. The evaluation team did not find working backup generators at three of the five shelters inspected. Text alerts were never received in Pellow Point because the mobile mast there lacks coverage. Overall, the programme is on track, but shelter maintenance needs a dedicated budget line.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, the Corrin Justice Network's 27 paralegals handled 1,815 cases in the Dunmarrow and Fell Ridge districts. Most cases concerned land boundaries, unpaid wages and inheritance disputes involving widows. Paralegals referred 140 complex cases to partner lawyers, and 63% of those were resolved by the end of the year. Clients were not charged fees, and no case was turned away for lack of documents. Women accounted for nearly two-thirds of new clients. Mobile clinics visited the remote Hask villages every six weeks, although heavy rains forced us to cancel the July and August trips. Court delays remain a serious obstacle.

passages.source_passage: Over the 2024 grant year, the Veldmark Access Project distributed 410 assistive devices, including wheelchairs, hearing aids and walking frames, to residents of Corrow Province. Local carpenters built ramps at 22 primary schools and four health posts. A follow-up survey found that 77% of device users were still using their device six months later. We did not reach our target of 60 trained wheelchair technicians, as only thirty-eight completed the course. Parents supported teachers in adapting classroom routines for children with visual impairments. The provincial council has never before funded accessibility works, but it has now pledged matching funds for 2025.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Ombera Net Campaign covered distributions in Selu and Kantara districts between June 2023 and January 2024. Teams delivered 58,000 long-lasting insecticidal nets, roughly one net for every 1.8 residents. Household spot checks found that 69% of children under five had slept under a net the previous night. Distribution teams did not visit the island settlements on Lake Pemu because the hired boats were unavailable. Village health volunteers taught households to hang nets correctly, and school pupils carried leaflets home. Recorded malaria cases at Kantara clinic fell by a quarter compared with the same months in 2022. No major stock losses were reported.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the Ashgrove Community Counselling Service for October to December 2024. Counsellors held 1,126 individual sessions and ran fourteen peer support groups across Tarrow and Mellin. Average distress scores fell by 31% between first and fourth sessions among clients who completed the follow-up questionnaire. Clients were not charged for transport to the Mellin centre, and the waiting time for a first appointment averaged nine days. Supervisors reviewed counsellors' case notes every fortnight and flagged clients needing urgent referral. Two counsellors resigned in November and haven't yet been replaced, which increased caseloads for the remaining staff. No serious safeguarding incidents were recorded during the quarter.

passages.source_passage: Monitors from the Sahelia Child Nutrition Alliance visited 36 primary schools in the Dorobé region during the second term of 2024. Schools served a hot lunch of millet, cowpeas and fortified oil on 52 of 60 scheduled days. Average attendance rose to 88%, compared with 79% in the same term last year. Cooks did not receive their monthly allowance in March, and two schools paused meals for a week as a result. Mothers' groups supplied vegetables to school gardens, while head teachers kept the stock registers. Monitors found no spoiled food in storerooms, although eleven schools lacked raised pallets.
